senses.def: full of light or shining strongly
examples: It was a bright, sunny morning.
The lights were so bright that I had to close my eyes.

senses.def: strong and easy to see
examples: She painted the kitchen a bright yellow.

senses.def: intelligent and quick to learn; likely to be successful
examples: He's a bright student with a bright future ahead of him.

note: "Look on the bright side" means focus on the good parts of a bad situation.

senses.def: extremely intelligent, skilled, or impressive
examples: She's a brilliant scientist who has won several awards.
That's a brilliant idea!

senses.def: very bright
examples: The sky turned a brilliant orange at sunset.

note: In British English "brilliant!" casually means "great!"; Americans more often say "awesome" or "great".

senses.def: to take someone or something with you to the place where you are going or where the speaker is
examples: Can you bring a salad to the party?
Don't forget to bring your passport.

senses.def: to cause a particular situation or feeling
examples: The new factory will bring hundreds of jobs to the area.
Her music brings joy to millions of people.

note: Irregular verb: bring – brought – brought. Bring = toward the speaker; take = away from the speaker.

senses.def: wide from one side to the other
examples: He has broad shoulders from years of swimming.
A broad river runs through the valley.

senses.def: including many different things or people; general rather than detailed
examples: The store offers a broad range of products.
There is broad agreement on the main goals.

note: "In broad daylight" means openly during the day, used about surprising crimes. Opposite: narrow.

senses.def: a fast internet connection that is always on
examples: Many rural homes still don't have access to broadband.
We upgraded to faster broadband so we could stream movies.

note: Common in news and policy language. In everyday American speech, people often just say "high-speed internet".

senses.def: to send out a program on television, radio, or the internet
examples: The game will be broadcast live on national TV.
The station broadcasts news every hour.

senses.def: a program sent out on television, radio, or the internet
examples: Millions watched the live broadcast of the ceremony.

note: Past forms are usually the same: broadcast – broadcast – broadcast.

senses.def: a person who presents programs on radio or television
examples: She worked as a sports broadcaster for twenty years.

senses.def: a company that sends out radio or television programs
examples: The public broadcaster refused to air the controversial ad.

senses.def: in a general way, without paying attention to details
examples: Broadly speaking, the plan was a success.
The two reports are broadly similar.

senses.def: with a wide smile
examples: He smiled broadly when he heard the good news.

senses.def: damaged, cracked, or no longer working properly
examples: Be careful, there's broken glass on the floor.
He's been off work with a broken leg.

senses.def: ended or destroyed, especially a relationship or promise
examples: She grew up in a broken home.
Voters are tired of broken promises.

note: "Broken English" means English spoken with many mistakes. For machines, Americans also say "out of order".

senses.def: a boy or man who has the same parents as you
examples: My older brother lives in Ankara.
She has two brothers and a sister.

note: English doesn't separate abi and küçük kardeş; say "older" or "younger brother". "Big Brother" also means government surveillance.

senses.def: having the color of soil or coffee
examples: She has long brown hair and green eyes.
Use brown sugar for a richer flavor.

senses.def: the color of soil or coffee
examples: The living room is decorated in warm browns and creams.

senses.def: to cook food until it turns brown on the outside
examples: Brown the onions in a little oil before adding the meat.

note: "Brown bread" and "brown rice" mean whole-grain.

senses.def: a computer program used to find and view pages on the internet
examples: Try clearing your browser history if the page won't load.
The website works in every major browser.

note: Related verb "browse" also means look around a store without a clear plan to buy.

senses.def: a tool with stiff hairs or wires on a handle, used for cleaning, painting, or hair
examples: Use a small brush to paint the corners.
She keeps a hair brush in her bag.

senses.def: to clean or tidy something with a brush
examples: Brush your teeth twice a day.
He brushed the snow off the car.

senses.def: to touch something lightly while moving past it
examples: Her hand brushed mine as she reached for the menu.

note: "Brush up on" means improve a skill you have partly forgotten: I need to brush up on my Spanish.

senses.def: very violent and cruel
examples: The country suffered under a brutal dictatorship.
Police are investigating a brutal attack in the park.

senses.tr: çok sert, dayanılmaz; (dürüstlük) kaba ama net
senses.def: very harsh or unpleasant; direct without trying to be kind
examples: The winter was brutal, with weeks of freezing temperatures.
I appreciated her brutal honesty about my essay.

note: "Brutally honest" means honest in a way that may hurt. "Police brutality" is a common news phrase.

senses.def: a ball of air or gas inside a liquid, or floating in the air
examples: The kids were blowing soap bubbles in the yard.
Small bubbles rose to the top of the glass.

senses.def: a situation where prices rise very fast and then suddenly fall
examples: Many investors lost everything when the housing bubble burst.

senses.def: a closed group or situation that keeps you away from other views or realities
examples: Social media can trap you in a bubble of people who think like you.

note: "Bubbly" describes a cheerful, lively person.

senses.def: (informal) a US dollar
examples: I bought this jacket for twenty bucks at a thrift store.
Can you lend me a few bucks for lunch?

senses.def: a male deer, rabbit, or similar animal
examples: A large buck stood at the edge of the forest.

note: Informal. "Pass the buck" = avoid responsibility by blaming others. "More bang for your buck" = better value.

senses.def: (informal) a friend
examples: I'm going camping with some buddies from college.
He and his workout buddy meet at the gym every morning.

senses.def: (informal, American) used to address a man, sometimes in an unfriendly way
examples: Hey buddy, you dropped your wallet!

note: Very common in American English. "Mate" is the British and Australian equivalent.

senses.def: the amount of money a person or organization has and a plan for spending it
examples: We have a budget of five hundred dollars for the trip.
The city council approved next year's budget.

senses.def: to plan carefully how much money to spend
examples: I budget about two hundred dollars a month for groceries.

senses.def: cheap
examples: We flew with a budget airline to save money.

senses.def: something that protects against harm or reduces the effect of a problem
examples: Savings act as a buffer against unexpected expenses.
Leave a buffer of thirty minutes in case of traffic.

senses.def: (of a video) to pause while more data loads
examples: The video kept buffering because the Wi-Fi was slow.

note: A "buffer zone" is a neutral area between two opposing countries or forces.

senses.def: (informal) any small insect
examples: There were bugs everywhere after the rain.
A bug flew into my coffee.

senses.def: a mistake in a computer program that stops it working correctly
examples: The update fixed a bug that made the app crash.

senses.def: (informal) a minor illness caused by an infection
examples: Half the office has caught a stomach bug.

senses.def: (informal) to annoy someone
examples: It really bugs me when people are late.

note: "Bug" as a verb also means put a secret microphone somewhere: The room was bugged.

senses.def: to make something by putting parts or materials together
examples: They're building a new hospital downtown.
My grandfather built this house himself.

senses.def: to develop something gradually, such as a relationship or business
examples: It takes years to build trust with customers.
She built her company from nothing.

senses.def: the shape and size of someone's body
examples: He has a strong, athletic build.

note: Irregular verb: build – built – built. "Build on" means use past success as a base for more.

senses.def: a structure with walls and a roof, such as a house or office
examples: The tallest building in the city has eighty floors.
Smoking is not allowed anywhere in the building.

senses.def: the process or business of constructing things
examples: The building of the new stadium took three years.

note: "Building blocks" are the basic parts that something is made from.

senses.def: the main or largest part of something
examples: The bulk of the work was done by volunteers.
Rent takes up the bulk of my salary.

senses.def: large quantities (used in "in bulk")
examples: Buying rice in bulk is much cheaper.

senses.def: the large size or weight of something or someone
examples: Despite his bulk, he moved surprisingly fast.

note: "The bulk of" is formal but very common in news and academic writing.

senses.def: a small piece of metal fired from a gun
examples: The bullet missed him by inches.
Police found several bullets at the scene.

note: "Bite the bullet" = do something unpleasant you've been avoiding. "Bullet points" are the dots in a list.

senses.def: a number of similar things growing or tied together
examples: He bought her a bunch of flowers.
Grab a bunch of bananas from the store.

senses.def: (informal) a large amount or group of people or things
examples: I have a whole bunch of emails to answer.
They're a nice bunch of people.

note: "A bunch of" for "a lot of" is very common in spoken American English: a bunch of stuff.

senses.def: a difficult duty or responsibility that causes worry or hard work
examples: The new tax will place a heavy burden on small businesses.
She didn't want to be a burden to her children.

senses.def: to give someone a duty or problem that is difficult to deal with
examples: I don't want to burden you with my problems.

note: "The burden of proof" is a legal phrase: the duty to prove something is true.

senses.def: a system of official rules and procedures, especially when it seems too slow or complicated
examples: Getting a work visa involves a lot of bureaucracy.
The new mayor promised to cut red tape and bureaucracy.

senses.def: the officials and departments that run a government or large organization
examples: The federal bureaucracy employs millions of people.

note: Usually negative. Spelling is tricky: bureau + cracy. "Red tape" is the informal equivalent.

senses.def: the act or ceremony of putting a dead body in the ground
examples: The burial took place in the family's hometown.
Archaeologists discovered an ancient burial site.

note: Pronounced /ˈberiəl/, like "berry-al", not "bury-al" with /ʌ/.

senses.def: to be on fire, or to destroy or damage something with fire or heat
examples: The old barn burned to the ground.
I burned the toast again.

senses.def: to use fuel or energy
examples: A brisk walk burns about three hundred calories an hour.

senses.def: an injury or mark caused by fire, heat, or acid
examples: She suffered minor burns on her hands while cooking.

note: Past form: burned (American) or burnt (British; also used as an adjective in American: burnt toast). "Burnout" = exhaustion from work.

senses.def: to break open suddenly because of pressure from inside, or to make something do this
examples: A water pipe burst in the basement during the cold night.
The balloon burst with a loud bang.

senses.def: to move or start doing something suddenly and with force
examples: The kids burst into the room shouting.
She burst into tears when she heard the news.

senses.def: a short, sudden period of activity, energy, or noise
examples: He finished the race with a final burst of speed.

note: Irregular verb: burst – burst – burst. "Bursting with" means very full of: bursting with pride.

senses.def: to put a dead body in the ground
examples: He was buried next to his wife in the village cemetery.

senses.def: to hide something in the ground or under other things
examples: Dogs often bury bones in the backyard to save them for later.
The report was buried under a pile of papers on my desk.

note: Pronounced /ˈberi/, same as "berry". "Bury the hatchet" means end an argument and become friends again.

senses.def: a large vehicle that carries passengers along a fixed route
examples: I take the bus to work every morning.
We missed the last bus and had to walk home.

note: Say "on the bus" (not "in the bus") and "by bus" (no article). Plural: buses.

senses.def: a plant like a small tree with many stems growing close together
examples: The cat was hiding behind a bush in the yard.
We planted rose bushes along the fence.

note: "Beat around the bush" means avoid saying something directly (Turkish: lafı dolandırmak).

senses.def: the activity of making, buying, and selling goods or services for money
examples: She studied business at college.
Business has been slow since the holidays.

senses.def: a company, store, or other organization that makes money
examples: He runs a small business that repairs bikes.

senses.def: something that concerns a particular person
examples: How much I earn is none of your business.

note: Pronounced /ˈbɪznəs/ with two syllables. "On business" means traveling for work.

senses.def: a man who works in business, especially one who owns or runs a company
examples: A local businessman donated money to rebuild the library.
He became a successful businessman by thirty.

note: Plural: businessmen. Gender-neutral options: businessperson, business owner, entrepreneur.

senses.def: having a lot of things to do and little free time
examples: I'm too busy to go out tonight.
She's busy working on her thesis.

senses.def: full of people, traffic, or activity
examples: The restaurant gets really busy on Friday nights.
They live on a busy street.

senses.def: (American) of a phone line, being used
examples: I tried calling, but the line was busy.

note: Pattern: busy + -ing (busy cooking), not "busy to cook". British English says the line is "engaged".

senses.def: used to introduce something that contrasts with what was just said
examples: The hotel was expensive but very comfortable.
I'd love to come, but I have to work.

senses.def: except; apart from
examples: Everyone but my brother came to the wedding.
I've had nothing but problems with this car.

note: "All but" means "almost" (all but impossible); "anything but" means "definitely not" (anything but easy).

senses.def: a soft yellow food made from cream, used in cooking and spread on bread
examples: Spread some butter on the toast while it's hot.
Melt the butter in a pan over low heat.

senses.def: to spread butter on something
examples: She buttered the bread and added a slice of cheese.

note: "Butter someone up" means be very nice to someone to get something. Uncountable: some butter.

senses.def: a small round object sewn onto clothes to fasten them
examples: A button fell off my coat on the way to work.

senses.def: a small part of a machine or screen that you press to make it work
examples: Press the red button to stop the machine.
Click the button below to download the file.

senses.def: to fasten clothes with buttons
examples: Button up your jacket; it's freezing outside.

collocations: at the push of a button
note: "Push someone's buttons" means deliberately annoy them.

senses.def: to get something by paying money for it
examples: We want to buy a house next year.
Did you buy anything at the mall?

senses.def: (informal) to believe something someone says
examples: He said the dog ate his homework, but the teacher didn't buy it.

senses.def: something you buy, especially at a good price
examples: At that price, the laptop is a really good buy.

note: Irregular verb: buy – bought – bought. "Buy time" means delay something to get more time.

senses.def: used to show how something is done, or who does it
examples: We traveled to Boston by train.
The novel was written by a young Nigerian author.

senses.def: not later than a particular time
examples: Please send me the report by Friday.

senses.def: near or beside someone or something
examples: She was sitting by the window reading a book.

senses.def: past someone or something
examples: A police car drove by with its lights flashing.
Time goes by so fast.

note: "By Friday" = no later than Friday; "until Friday" = continuing up to Friday.

senses.def: (informal) goodbye
examples: Bye! See you tomorrow.
She waved bye to her friends from the bus window.

note: Informal. "Bye-bye" sounds childish or very casual.

senses.def: a small room for sleeping on a ship, or the area where passengers sit on a plane
examples: Our cabin on the cruise ship had a small window.
The cabin crew served drinks after takeoff.

senses.def: a small, simple wooden house, especially in the woods or mountains
examples: We rented a log cabin by the lake for the weekend.

note: "Cabin fever" is the restless feeling from being stuck indoors too long.

senses.def: a group of senior government members who make important decisions
examples: The president announced several changes to his cabinet.
She served in the cabinet as secretary of state.

senses.def: a piece of furniture with shelves or drawers, used for storing things
examples: The glasses are in the kitchen cabinet above the sink.

note: A "cabinet reshuffle" is when a leader changes which ministers do which jobs.

senses.def: a set of wires covered in plastic that carries electricity or signals
examples: Plug the cable into the back of the TV.
Workers are laying fiber-optic cables under the street.

senses.def: a television system that sends programs through cables
examples: Many young people cancel cable and just use streaming services.

note: A "cable car" (teleferik) is pulled by a cable up a hill or mountain.

senses.def: a small place where you can buy drinks and simple meals
examples: Let's meet at the cafe across from the library.
She spends hours working on her laptop in cafes.

note: Also spelled "café". Americans often say "coffee shop". A "cafeteria" is a self-service restaurant, e.g. in a school.

senses.def: a sweet baked food made from flour, eggs, sugar, and butter
examples: We ordered a chocolate cake for her birthday.
Would you like another slice of cake?

collocations: have your cake and eat it too
note: "A piece of cake" means very easy. "Cake" covers both Turkish "pasta" and "kek"; "pasta" in English means noodles.

senses.def: to find a number or amount using mathematics
examples: Use this app to calculate how much tax you owe.
Scientists calculated the distance to the star.

senses.def: to judge or guess what will probably happen
examples: We calculated that the trip would take about four hours.

note: A "calculated risk" is one taken after careful thought. A "calculating" person is coldly selfish.

senses.def: the process of using numbers to find an amount, or the result of this
examples: By my calculation, we'll run out of money in March.
The engineers made a few mistakes in their calculations.

senses.def: careful planning to get what you want, often in a selfish way
examples: Her kindness seemed to be based on cold calculation.

senses.def: to phone someone
examples: I'll call you when I get to the airport.
Call 911 if anyone is hurt.

senses.def: to give someone or something a name, or to describe them in a certain way
examples: They called their daughter Elif after her grandmother.
Critics called the plan a disaster.

senses.def: an act of speaking to someone on the phone
examples: I got a call from the bank this morning.

senses.def: a public request for something to happen
examples: There are growing calls for the minister to resign.

note: "Call off" = cancel. "A close call" = a narrow escape from danger. "It's your call" = it's your decision.
